question:
An engineer implements a Cisco UCS C-Series Server that must adhere to these security requirements:
- Unencrypted communication must be disabled.
- The session timeout must not exceed 15 minutes.
- Unencrypted traffic must be automatically diverted.
- CLI-based management must use nondefault ports.
Which configuration set meets these requirements?
options: SSH Enabled SSH Port: 8022 SSH Timeout: 1200 IPMI over LAN Enabled
HTTP Port: 80 / HTTPS Port: 443 Session Timeout: 900 Redirect HTTP to HTTPS Enabled SSH Port: 2022
Redfish Enabled checked Redfish Port: 443 SSH Enabled checked HTTPS Port: 8443
XML API Enabled HTTP Port: 8080 / HTTPS Port: 8443 IPMI over LAN Enabled Randomized Encryption Key
explanation: Only choice B meets all the requirements given of timing out in 15 minutes (900 seconds), Redirecting HTTP to HTTPS, and using a non-default SSH port.
theory: Hardening Cisco IMC out-of-band management to meet 'encrypt everything, 15-minute timeout, auto-redirect unencrypted traffic, nondefault CLI ports' requires enabling HTTPS with HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, setting the session timeout to 900 seconds (15 minutes, versus the 1800-second/30-minute default), and moving SSH off its default port 22 to a custom port. Cisco IMC ships with HTTP port 80/HTTPS 443 and SSH port 22 by default, so every one of these values must be explicitly changed to satisfy the policy. (Cisco documentation / web research - Cisco UCS C-Series Integrated Management Controller CLI Configuration Guide)
